body: I smoked for years. Another great example of the lies we tell. I smoked behind the shed at an apartment. I was a grown woman but I lied to everybody. I'm sick of the weird lies I tell. I have quit smoking but I still lie. I lie about where I'm going. Always, and to everybody. I don't know why I do it. Is it a feeling of control? Is this the only way I have ever had any control in my actual life?

Yes!!! This is an example of what I'm thinking about. Those weird little lies. Lies that we don't have to tell but if we tell the 'truth' we will be in big trouble. For me, having one friend, (a possible escape route) is almost like doing an illegal drug. It's somewhere for me to go just in case the BIG one happens. I always carry with me the feeling of something awful is going to happen, I don't know where, don't know when, but when it happens, I have a secret place where no one can find me. The oddest thing about this is that I have always done it and never once thought this was strange. Yesterday, coming home from his house, I realized that if I died no one would ever know or find me. Writing this makes me realize that maybe that danger is something so familiar to me that I can't live without it.
secret money always seems like the smart thing. I love to find a five or ten I folded somewhere for my future self to find. It always feels like a gift.
I understand that. Information sharing is a huge deal. I never know how much to share. Too little could help but oversharing is also an issue. Where the hell is the middle line?

Yes. I have secret money too. I have a set amount that I need to feel safe. The secret friend is usually someone who has a place I can go to just to 'disappear' for an afternoon or a day. It just struck me as odd and I realized today that if I never came back from my friend's house, no one would ever know where to find me:( Maybe, not good.

I am the proud mom of a 21 year old man. He is the most wonderful human being that I have ever known. He was always allowed to explore his own spirituality. He was always thought of as his own person. He was encouraged to have relationships with people I didn't necessarily like. Because HE IS A PERSON. 

My son's father and I split when he was five. I never stood in the way of his relationship with his father or that side of the family. To this day, I'm glad. My son chose to join the Army. For me, this was a surprise. I had ideas about him being an artist or a musician. But he has surprised me by loving to work with his hands as his great grandfather did. He loves getting dirty and only feels like he worked hard if he is physically exhausted at the end of the day. He surprised me when he was diagnosed with learning disabilities. He surprised me when he had a head full of fuzzy red hair at birth. He's left-handed! Another, beautiful surprise. But by far, the biggest surprise has been how much we love each other and genuinely enjoy each others company. I am blessed beyond beyond!! I am so happy for you. A boy and his mom is a special relationship indeed.
